products.name: Contoured (3D) sleep mask
products.bestFor: Side sleepers and anyone who dislikes pressure on the eyes
products.keyFeature: Moulded eye cups that sit around, not on, the eyes
products.description: A contoured mask has raised eye cups so the fabric does not press on your eyelids, which many people find more comfortable and which allows the eyes to move freely in REM sleep. Manta's version is marketed with adjustable eye cups and a wide, flat strap designed to reduce light leaks.
products.why: The main failure of a cheap flat mask is light leaking in around the nose. A contoured design with an adjustable strap closes that gap for more face shapes.
products.consideration: Bulkier than a flat mask, so less convenient for travel.

products.name: Silk sleep mask
products.bestFor: Comfort against the skin, warm sleepers, travel
products.description: Flat masks made from mulberry silk are marketed for comfort and breathability and are light enough to pack easily. They rely on a soft fit rather than eye cups.
products.why: If you find fabric on the eyelids fine and simply want something light and cool, silk is a comfortable option, though flat masks tend to leak more light around the nose than contoured ones.
products.consideration: Less light-blocking at the edges than a contoured mask; hand-wash care.

products.name: Weighted sleep mask
products.bestFor: People who like gentle pressure across the face
products.keyFeature: Light, evenly distributed weight (typically filled with glass beads)
products.description: Weighted masks add a small amount of even pressure across the forehead and eyes. Manufacturers market them for relaxation; evidence for a sleep benefit specific to weighted masks is limited.
products.why: Some people find the pressure calming in the same way a heavy duvet feels comforting. It is a preference rather than a proven benefit.
products.consideration: Not suited to back-sleeper-only designs if you turn a lot; heavier to travel with.

products.name: Soft foam earplugs
products.bestFor: Maximum noise reduction at low cost
products.keyFeature: Slow-recovery foam that expands to seal the ear canal
products.description: Foam plugs are compressed, inserted and allowed to expand. Mack's Ultra Soft are marketed as a low-pressure foam intended for sleeping and are sold in multi-packs. Foam plugs are single- or few-use and should be replaced regularly.
products.why: For steady noise such as traffic or a partner's snoring, a well-fitted foam plug usually gives the greatest reduction of the common types.
products.consideration: Can feel bulky for side sleepers; disposable, so the cost adds up; check the SNR rating on the pack.

products.name: Reusable silicone earplugs for sleep
products.bestFor: Side sleepers and people who want a washable, reusable option
products.keyFeature: Low-profile, flexible silicone with interchangeable tip sizes
products.description: Loop Quiet earplugs are marketed as reusable silicone plugs with a round, low-profile shape and several ear-tip sizes in the box. Manufacturer information describes them as intended for sleep, focus and noise sensitivity.
products.why: They sit flatter than foam, so they are less likely to press into the ear on a pillow, and they can be washed rather than thrown away.
products.consideration: Generally a little less noise reduction than a well-inserted foam plug; fit depends on choosing the right tip size.

products.name: Mouldable wax or silicone putty earplugs
products.brandExample: Quies natural wax earplugs; Mack's Pillow Soft silicone
products.bestFor: People who find in-canal plugs uncomfortable
products.keyFeature: Soft putty that moulds over the entrance to the ear canal
products.description: Putty-style plugs are pressed over the ear opening rather than inserted into the canal. Wax versions (such as Quies) and silicone versions (such as Mack's Pillow Soft) are both marketed for sleep and swimming.
products.why: Because nothing goes inside the canal, many people find them the most comfortable option for side sleeping, and they seal well when applied properly.
products.consideration: Single-use or short-life; can pick up hair and lint; less suited to very loud environments.

products.name: Fan-based white noise machine
products.bestFor: People who want natural, non-looping white noise
products.keyFeature: A real internal fan creates the sound, so there is no digital loop
products.description: The Dohm is a long-established design that uses an enclosed fan and adjustable vents to produce a steady, fan-like sound. The manufacturer markets it as having two speeds with tone adjusted by rotating the housing.
products.why: Digital machines can have audible loop points that some people notice. A fan-based machine produces continuous sound with no loop, and no need for a screen or app.
products.consideration: One type of sound only (no brown or pink noise options); uses mains power; check the UK plug version.

products.name: Digital sound machine with multiple noise colours
products.bestFor: Choice of white, pink and brown-style sounds and fan sounds
products.keyFeature: Non-looping digitally generated noise with many variants and a timer
products.description: LectroFan machines are marketed as producing a range of fan sounds and white-noise variations digitally, with the manufacturer stating the sounds are generated rather than recorded loops. They include a timer and volume control.
products.why: If you want to experiment with brown or pink noise rather than only white, a multi-sound digital machine lets you find the tone that suits you best.
products.consideration: Some people prefer the softer character of a fan-based machine; check the UK power adapter.

products.name: Portable rechargeable sound machine
products.keyFeature: Small, rechargeable, a few sound options
products.description: Portable machines are marketed for travel, running on a rechargeable battery with a small selection of sounds. They are typically designed to be packed in a bag or clipped to luggage.
products.why: Unfamiliar rooms are often the noisiest, and a small machine means you are not relying on a phone that may need charging or buzz with notifications.
products.consideration: Smaller speakers can sound thinner at higher volumes; fewer sounds than a full-size machine.

products.name: Headband sleep headphones
products.bestFor: Side sleepers who want audio without anything inside the ear
products.keyFeature: Thin, flat speakers inside a soft fabric headband
products.description: Headband headphones put flat speakers inside a stretchy fabric band that doubles as a light-blocking eye cover for some people. Models are marketed as wired or Bluetooth, with the speakers usually removable so the band can be washed.
products.why: Ordinary earbuds press into the ear when you lie on your side. A headband keeps the speaker flat against the ear so you can listen to sleep sounds or guided relaxation comfortably.
products.consideration: Audio quality is basic and bass-light; the band can feel warm in summer; battery life varies by model.

products.name: Small in-ear sleep earbuds
products.brandExample: Anker Soundcore Sleep series; Bose Sleepbuds (discontinued, second-hand only)
products.bestFor: People who want noise masking and audio in a compact form
products.keyFeature: Low-profile earbuds designed to sit flush with the ear
products.description: Sleep-specific earbuds are marketed as smaller and flatter than standard earbuds so that lying on a pillow does not push them into the ear. Some models are designed mainly for masking sounds via an app; check whether a model streams normal Bluetooth audio if that matters to you.
products.why: They combine some passive noise blocking with audio, which suits people who want both a plug and a sound in one device.
products.consideration: Fit varies widely between ears; app dependence on some models; batteries degrade over time.

products.name: Memory foam pillow for side sleepers
products.brandExample: Various UK brands (e.g. Simba Hybrid, Emma, Panda)
products.bestFor: Side sleepers who need a higher, firmer pillow to keep the neck level
products.keyFeature: Supportive foam with enough loft to fill the gap between shoulder and head
products.description: Memory foam pillows are marketed for their contouring support and stable height. Several UK brands offer adjustable versions where foam layers or pieces can be removed to change the height.
products.why: Side sleepers generally need more height than back sleepers. An adjustable foam pillow lets you fine-tune the loft rather than guessing.
products.consideration: Foam can sleep warm; new pillows sometimes have an initial smell that fades; check the trial and return terms.

products.name: Gel-layer cooling pillow
products.bestFor: Hot sleepers who like foam support
products.keyFeature: Gel-infused or gel-layered foam marketed to draw heat away from the head
products.description: Cooling pillows commonly combine memory foam with a gel layer or gel-infused foam, and are marketed as feeling cooler to the touch. The cooling effect is usually most noticeable at first contact rather than all night.
products.why: If you wake up hot, the pillow is one of the warmest contact points. A breathable or gel-layered pillow paired with a cool room can help.
products.consideration: Cooling claims vary and are hard to compare; a breathable cover and cool room matter as much as the pillow itself.

products.name: Thermal blackout curtains (eyelet)
products.bestFor: Bedrooms with street lights or early summer dawn
products.keyFeature: Multi-layer or coated fabric marketed to block most light and reduce heat loss
products.description: Blackout curtains use a dense or coated backing to block light. Thermal versions are also marketed for insulation, which can help in winter and keep rooms slightly cooler in summer when closed during the day.
products.why: Curtains address the room rather than the person, so they help everyone in the bed and do not need to be worn.
products.consideration: Light still leaks around the edges and top unless the curtains overlap the frame generously; measure carefully.

products.name: No-drill blackout blind
products.bestFor: Renters, travel cots, and windows where curtains leave gaps
products.keyFeature: Fits inside the window recess without drilling
products.description: Portable or no-drill blackout blinds attach with suction cups or tension fittings and are marketed for rented homes and travel. Some are cut to size.
products.why: Fitting inside the recess blocks the edge glow that curtains let through. Combined with curtains, the room can get very dark.
products.consideration: Suction fittings may need re-fixing; less tidy-looking than fitted blinds.

products.name: Weighted blanket (glass-bead fill)
products.brandExample: Various UK brands (e.g. Mela, Gravity, Silentnight)
products.bestFor: People who find gentle, even pressure calming
products.keyFeature: Quilted pockets of glass beads distributing weight evenly
products.description: Weighted blankets are typically filled with fine glass beads sewn into small pockets. Manufacturers commonly suggest choosing a weight around 10% of body weight. Some evidence suggests benefits for anxiety and sleep in certain groups; it is not a treatment for any condition.
products.why: If a heavy duvet already feels comforting, a weighted blanket gives that sensation year-round without the heat of extra duvets.
products.consideration: Not suitable for young children or people with certain respiratory or mobility conditions; can be warm; heavy to wash.

products.name: Cotton percale bedding
products.description: Percale is a plain cotton weave marketed for its crisp, cool feel compared with the smoother, warmer sateen weave. It is widely available in UK sizes.
products.why: Fabric affects how much heat and moisture stays next to you. Percale or linen tends to feel cooler than polyester or sateen.
products.consideration: Wrinkles more than sateen; check thread count claims with caution as they are not a quality guarantee.

products.name: Lightweight summer duvet (around 4.5 tog)
products.keyFeature: Low tog rating for minimal insulation
products.description: Tog is the UK measure of a duvet's warmth. Duvets around 4.5 tog are marketed as summer weight; all-season sets combine a summer and a mid-weight duvet that clip together for winter.
products.why: Swapping a 13.5 tog winter duvet for a summer weight one is one of the simplest ways to stop waking up hot.
products.consideration: Fill (down, feather, microfibre, wool) affects breathability as much as tog.

products.name: Quiet bedroom fan
products.brandExample: Various (pedestal or desk fans marketed as quiet or with a night mode)
products.bestFor: Hot nights in homes without air conditioning
products.keyFeature: Low noise at low speeds, timer or night mode
products.description: Bedroom fans marketed as 'quiet' typically advertise low decibel levels at their lowest settings and often include a timer. A fan moves air rather than cooling it, so it helps most when air can also be exchanged with a cooler room or outside.
products.why: Airflow over the skin helps sweat evaporate, which is how the body cools. A fan also produces steady sound that masks other noise.
products.consideration: Noise levels are self-reported by manufacturers; in very hot, humid rooms a fan alone has limited effect.
